key_insight: Crystal-structure-dependent recrystallization produces hourglass-like ion tracks in rutile TiO2 but relatively uniform cylindrical tracks in anatase.
engineering_relevance: Understanding track recovery can guide irradiation-based modification of TiO2 and improve interpretation of radiation-damage microscopy.
method: Compare swift heavy ion damage in rutile and anatase TiO2.
Use TEM to characterize track morphology and electron-beam-induced changes.
Use molecular dynamics to examine recrystallization during rapid cooling.
evidence_signal: TEM observations show distinct track morphologies in the two polymorphs, while simulations attribute these differences to their recrystallization behavior.
watch_item: Prolonged TEM electron-beam exposure can recrystallize amorphous tracks and surface hillocks, altering the apparent damage morphology.
paper_title: Swift Heavy Ion Tracks in Polymorphs of Titanium Dioxide: The Effects of Electron Beam and Crystal Structures
